section.title: Staff engineering begins with leadership beyond your own tasks
section.deck: Peterman introduces staff engineering through scope, influence, and the individual-contributor career path.

blocks.text: Peterman describes a common progression from entry-level through mid-level to senior engineering. At many companies, senior can be a sustainable destination as well as a branching point: an engineer may continue on the individual-contributor ladder or move into management. He presents this as a broad framing, not a universal set of titles or a guarantee that every company organizes careers the same way.
blocks.heading: A career branch, not an obligatory next promotion

blocks.text: In his framing, staff is the first individual-contributor level at which leadership is unavoidable. You can remain an engineer without becoming a people manager, but you must help other people and projects succeed. The promotion is difficult precisely because it is a change in scope and behavior, not merely recognition for writing more code.
blocks.heading: Lead while remaining an individual contributor

blocks.text: He emphasizes the unusual scope of the engineering path: tools, systems, and methods can increase the effectiveness of both an individual and many other people. This creates a route to greater influence and compensation outside management. His comparison with other professions is an illustration of that idea, rather than a comprehensive claim about their career ladders.
